description: We are two families from Murcia, Spain: two mothers and four young participants. We enjoy space exploration, science and creative storytelling. We plan to create an engaging story about NASA equipment left on the Moon or Mars for a school-age audience. Our team is already complete.
summary:
Cosmo Tribu Murcia: as part of our challenge to recover and tell the story of equipment abandoned on the Moon and Mars by NASA, we’ve created a rock band called ‘Los Nas-ing Stones’, featuring AI characters, just like other bands that appeal to children and young people. The idea came to us because the youngest member of our team was wearing a Rolling Stones T-shirt.
The “Nas-ing Stones” will star in a series of missions designed to give purpose and visibility to all these abandoned objects featured in our challenge.
They could go viral and become known around the world if NASA selects our idea.
For our exhibition, we showcase what the band and its members are like, and we focus on an initial mission involving a very important piece of equipment: the “Ingenuity” helicopter. We use drawings and comics featuring the band members to explain to children and young people, in an educational way, what the helicopter does. In addition, a tool has been developed to apply the benefits and technological advances of the space helicopter to Earth. Something similar could be used by converting it into a drone and fitting it with a thermal imaging camera to rescue people in the event of a natural disaster. This makes it easier to explain its usefulness on Mars. 
We also plan a chatbot, which all can use to ask all sorts of questions about NASA’s abandoned spacecraft.
The name “Nas-ing Stones” includes one letter from each team member’s name (Carlota, Jorge, Neus, Neus Jr., Luis and Esther).
details:
Our response to Challenge 1 has been to create an image that provides the perfect setting for explaining and raising awareness of the equipment abandoned by NASA. A virtual rock band, ‘Los Nas-ing Stones’, has a series of ‘missions’ – episodes in which it tells the story of each piece of equipment on Mars or the Moon. The formats used to bring these stories to life include video episodes, comics and songs, and a ‘chatbot’ will also be created to answer any questions asked; it will feature the images of the rock band members, who will be the ones responding.

The benefits are clear: through an educational format suitable for children and young people, technical content is made accessible to the general public. Directly from the NASA website or via social media platforms, it shares knowledge about the missions so they are not forgotten. To create a story as required by the challenge, the example of one of the missions – the Ingenuity helicopter – has been chosen.

The project could have a global impact; the chatbot can respond in many languages, just as the catchy songs and short videos about the missions do. The story of the first mission also utilises the camera from the helicopter that flew on Mars to find a practical use for it on Earth, transforming it into a drone and adding a thermal imaging camera to locate living beings during natural disasters. It is a feasible and easily understandable example to raise the profile of NASA and its teams and highlight their contribution to scientific progress.

Creativity permeates everything; Neus’s mother came up with the name inspired by her daughter Neus’s Rolling Stones T-shirt, and then everyone contributed ideas about the story of the helicopter and the rescue mission.

We are a multidisciplinary team, diverse in age and commitment. For this project, the children researched the information provided and used AI to create the images we wanted to showcase. Drawing on ideas from the song’s lyrics and our own beliefs, we champion and defend our concept and its development as our response to Challenge 1.

In the chatbot, children will be able to ask the band questions such as “How did Ingenuity find its way on Mars?” and “How did it help Perseverance?”

The name “Nas-ing Stones” includes one letter from each team member’s name (Carlota, Jorge, Neus, Neus Jr., Luis and Esther).
